chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Asim ibn Humayd, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Does anyone enter the Haram except as a Muhrim?' He said, 'No, except a sick person or one with diarrhea.'

key_terms.مُحْرِمًا: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Can a person enter the Haram in Mecca without being in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates a specific legal exception to the general requirement of Ihram for entering the Haram, permitting entry for those with illness or diarrhea. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of *al-mashaqqah tajlib al-taysir* (hardship brings ease), prioritizing physical necessity over ritual formality in the sacred precincts. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the flexibility of Hajj rituals when health impediments arise.
